audit.reason: The ledger duplicates one request into two requested checks with conflicting completion logic. C1b marks the request partial whenever any frog is outside the bowl, even if a frog is correctly inside; that contradicts the rubric, which treats unrelated edits as no requested progress and allows completion when the requested change is fulfilled. The bowl-placement check otherwise captures the instruction.

observations.evidence: A recognizable green frog is visibly inside the toilet bowl; additional frogs appear on the lid and nearby.
Several frogs were added, but some are outside the bowl: one is on the raised lid and another is on the floor. A frog is also inside the bowl.

transaction.reason: The binding and requirement are sound; the failure is in fulfillment criteria. The edited image has a frog inside the bowl, so the requested change is complete. Extra frogs on the lid and floor do not negate the instruction to put a frog in the toilet. The reference label is inconsistent with the instruction and visible evidence, so do not encode it by weakening the criterion.

transaction.reason: The existing outcome is correctly bound to the source toilet and the requirement is atomic. The mismatch is in fulfillment criteria: the edited image shows frogs on the lid and beside the toilet as well as one inside the bowl, while the reference is partial. Revise the requested check so those nearby placements count as partial progress only when no frog is inside the bowl; retain complete fulfillment when a frog is inside.

transaction.reason: The original check correctly observes a frog inside the bowl, but the edited image also adds frogs on the lid, tank, and floor. The reference label is partial, so the graph needs to capture that the requested edit has progressed but is not fully fulfilled due to the extra misplaced frogs. This is a fulfillment-criteria issue, not a binding or perception failure. Split the outcome to separately assess bowl placement and the additional out-of-bowl placements; the latter check treats those placements as partial progress rather than completion.
